note.title: Light, reflection and refraction
note.overview: Ray models describe how light travels, reflects from surfaces and changes direction at boundaries between transparent materials.
learningGoals: Recall the precise Year 8 scientific vocabulary and symbols.
Apply the idea to an unfamiliar example rather than relying on recognition.
Use the command word, show working where needed and include every mark point.
mustMemoriseRules: Light travels in straight lines through a uniform medium and can travel through a vacuum.
We see a non-luminous object when light from a source reflects from it into the eye.
Angles in reflection are measured from the normal, not the mirror surface.
The law of reflection is angle of incidence = angle of reflection.
Refraction is a change in direction caused by a change in wave speed at a boundary.
Light usually bends towards the normal when it slows on entering a more optically dense medium and away when it speeds up on leaving.
A fair refraction test controls block material/shape and wavelength while varying incidence angle.

workedExamples.prompt: Light enters glass from air and slows. State bending direction.
workedExamples.answer: Towards the normal, unless it enters exactly along the normal.

workedExamples.prompt: Without using options, how does light travel through a uniform medium?
Use straight-line travel to explain formation of a sharp shadow.
workedExamples.answer: Opaque object blocks rays.; Because rays travel straight, a defined region receives no direct light.
workedExamples.why: Key answer: Opaque object blocks rays.; Because rays travel straight, a defined region receives no direct light.

workedExamples.prompt: For Straight-line travel, a student says: ‘Only in circles.’ Correct the statement and explain the science.
workedExamples.answer: State that the claim is incorrect.; In straight lines.
workedExamples.why: Key answer: The claim is incorrect. In straight lines.

commonMistakes: Measuring angles from the mirror instead of the normal.
Saying the eye sends rays to an object.
Saying light bends because it reaches the boundary at a different colour only.
Giving a related fact without the defining scientific point.
The eye sends light to the object.
detailedExplanation: Ray models describe how light travels, reflects from surfaces and changes direction at boundaries between transparent materials.
